answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before voting on task quality, then slash the bond when independently verified fraud is reported. Voting weight is capped by bonded value, not account count, so splitting funds among aliases named lotus, jetty, and comet creates no extra influence. The attacker must immobilize more capital and risk losing it, making mass Sybils costly rather than free; this raises the cost of attack, but does not make it impossible.
